::: {.column width="53%"}
::: {.about-subtitle}
Hi! I'm **Olivia Jackson Lambert**. I lead the data team at Hockeystick, where I'm
responsible for the platform, the analytics, and the models other teams build on.

I came to leadership through building — physics first, then consulting, then campaign
data at national scale — and I still think the interesting part of this work is the
decision at the end of it, not the model in the middle.

When I’m not working, I’m usually kayaking, reading, making art, or hanging out with my husband and three cats.
:::
:::

## How I Work

```{=html}
<div class="principles">
  <div class="principle">
    <div class="principle-num">01</div>
    <div>
      <h4>Start from the decision</h4>
      <p>A model is only worth what it changes. Before building, I want to know what someone will actually do differently once the number exists — and if the answer is nothing, that's worth finding out early.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="principle">
    <div class="principle-num">02</div>
    <div>
      <h4>Name the trade-off</h4>
      <p>Every model gives something up. I'd rather say out loud what a choice costs — accuracy traded away to clear a safety threshold, say — than hand over a single score as though it came free.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="principle">
    <div class="principle-num">03</div>
    <div>
      <h4>Build for people who shouldn't have to ask</h4>
      <p>The measure of a data team isn't how fast it answers questions, it's how rarely anyone needs to ask. Self-serve tooling beats a shorter ticket queue every time.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="principle">
    <div class="principle-num">04</div>
    <div>
      <h4>Own the whole path</h4>
      <p>Cost, uptime and the state of the pipeline are part of the modelling work, not somebody else's problem downstream. A model nobody can run on a Tuesday morning isn't finished.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Highlights

```{=html}
<div class="card-grid">
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Building a team</h4>
    <p>Grew the data function from 3 to 7 across engineering, analytics and science, and shifted the culture toward one where people question assumptions and surface risks rather than just closing tickets.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Platform migration</h4>
    <p>Led the move off Civis onto Google Cloud and BigQuery, cutting $60K a year in platform spend and 50 hours a month of pipeline babysitting while holding 99.9% uptime.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Self-serve tooling</h4>
    <p>Took inbound data requests from around 300 a month to 5 by building internal analytics products in Next.js, so other teams could answer their own questions.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Modeling that moved revenue</h4>
    <p>Led a donor propensity modeling initiative that overhauled segmentation and targeting, increasing revenue from data acquisitions by 121%.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Reliable pipelines at scale</h4>
    <p>Released machine learning scores at the Democratic National Committee to 100K+ monthly users across 160+ million voter records, on dbt and Airflow.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Time-series forecasting</h4>
    <p>Built a global demand forecasting pipeline with Prophet and PySpark, delivering 10K+ forecasts every month to teams on five continents.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Computer vision in research</h4>
    <p>Analyzed hundreds of Type 1a supernova images from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, applying computer vision to study their local environments.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="card">
    <h4>Statistical methods in research</h4>
    <p>Modeled sampling approaches for Mars sample return missions to assess their feasibility and scientific value, published in <em>Nature Astronomy</em>.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```
